user_request: gpt-6-astra · Design an NPU for accelerating matrix-vector multiplication in neural-network inference. Use 16 parallel INT8 multiply-accumulate units, INT32 accumulators, optional bias addition, and selectable ReLU activation. The accelerator should accept input data and return results through ready/valid streaming interfaces.

rtl_context.user_request: gpt-6-astra · Design an NPU for accelerating matrix-vector multiplication in neural-network inference. Use 16 parallel INT8 multiply-accumulate units, INT32 accumulators, optional bias addition, and selectable ReLU activation. The accelerator should accept input data and return results through ready/valid streaming interfaces.

design.name: mv_npu_int8x16
design.description: Streaming matrix-vector INT8 inference accelerator with 16 parallel MACs, INT32 accumulation, optional bias add, selectable ReLU.

operations.name: dot_product_row
operations.semantics: For each output row r, compute acc_r = sum_{c=0..N-1}(A[r,c]*x[c]) using signed INT8 operands and signed INT32 accumulation.

operations.name: bias_add
operations.semantics: If cfg_bias_enable=1, y_pre = acc_r + bias[r]; else y_pre = acc_r.

operations.name: relu
operations.semantics: If cfg_relu_enable=1, y = max(0,y_pre); else y = y_pre.

data_types.name: int32_s
data_types.conversion_semantics: Products accumulated in INT32; optional bias add in INT32

data_objects.name: matrix_a_stream
data_objects.role: matrix elements A in row-major order

dimensions.name: M
dimensions.semantic: number of matrix rows / output length; runtime value from job_config; legal iff 1<=M<=MAX_M

dimensions.name: N
dimensions.semantic: number of matrix columns / input vector length; runtime value from job_config; legal iff 1<=N<=MAX_N

compute.dataflow: Row-stationary over A rows with local x buffer reuse
compute.parallelism: Up to LANES=16 multiplies per cycle during compute phase
compute.scheduling: Per job: load x (N beats), then for each row load A row chunked by LANES and accumulate; optional bias and relu on row finalize; stream out row result immediately

storage.name: x_buffer
storage.access_pattern: Sequential write during x load; random/strided read by column index during row compute
storage.port_requirements: 1W + 1R per cycle logical (dual-port RAM or equivalent)
storage.reuse_semantics: Loaded once per job, reused across all M rows
storage.lifetime: from x load completion until job completion

storage.name: acc_regfile
storage.access_pattern: read/modify/write each compute cycle for current row
storage.reuse_semantics: cleared at row start, finalized at row end

storage.name: a_lane_regs
storage.access_pattern: loaded each A-data beat then consumed same/next cycle

pipeline.responsibility: accept config and classify incoming stream sections
write x_buffer or lane/bias staging from input stream
16 parallel int8 multiplies + reduction + acc update
pipeline.stall_behavior: freeze acc and indices when downstream stall affects progress

pipeline.responsibility: optional bias, optional relu, drive output valid/data
pipeline.valid_behavior: emit one row result per successful output transfer

control.state_progression: IDLE->RECV_CFG->LOAD_X->COMPUTE_ROWS->DONE; within COMPUTE_ROWS iterate col_chunk then finalize row
control.error_behavior: If config has M or N out of legal range, enter ERROR and raise status_err; ignore input payload until new valid cfg accepted
control.error_recovery: From ERROR, accept next cfg transfer with legal bounds and transition to LOAD_X

reset.required_state: FSM=IDLE, counters=0, valid outputs deasserted, status_err=0, busy=0

architecture_contract.latency_model: Cycles = 1(cfg)+N(load_x)+sum_{r=0..M-1}(ceil(N/LANES)+row_finalize_and_output_wait). With no output backpressure and continuous input A/bias, row_finalize_and_output_wait=1.
architectural_invariants: Exactly one output produced per row.
x vector is loaded once per job and not required to be retransmitted during row compute.
Result order strictly row index ascending 0..M-1.
All transfers use ready&&valid semantics with stable payload while stalled.
open_assumptions: Single unified input data channel carries config, x, A, and optional bias sections distinguished by metadata type field.
A elements are provided row-major matching compute traversal.
Bias section is present iff cfg_bias_enable=1; absent otherwise.
INT32 overflow behavior is wraparound as user did not request saturation.

channels.name: in_cmd_data
channels.framing: Sections in strict order: CFG(1 beat) -> X(N beats) -> A(M*N beats) -> BIAS(M beats if enabled).
channels.ordering: Within A section row-major: A[0,0]..A[0,N-1], A[1,0]..

channels.name: out_result
channels.framing: Exactly M beats per job, one int32 per beat

signals.name: in_data
signals.semantic: payload: cfg packed on cfg beat; int8 value in bits[7:0] for X/A beats; int32 bias for BIAS beats

signals.name: out_last
signals.semantic: asserted with last output row beat

signals.name: status_err
signals.semantic: latched high in ERROR state, cleared on legal cfg accept

global_handshake_rules.stall_behavior: source must hold payload and metadata stable while valid=1 and ready=0

modules.name: input_router
modules.responsibility: Route input beats to cfg/x/a/bias sinks

ports.name: cfg_word
ports.semantics: assembled cfg over 1 beat using in_data plus zeros in upper bits

ports.name: a_lane_data
ports.semantics: packed lane A bytes; one lane used per beat in this simple schedule

modules.name: output_if
modules.responsibility: Output holding register and ready/valid handling

functional: For each legal job, output y[r]=ReLU_sel(sum_c(A[r,c]*x[c])+bias_sel) with exact integer arithmetic and declared wrap semantics.
If bias disabled, bias stream must not be required; if enabled, exactly M bias beats consumed.
If relu enabled, all negative outputs clamp to 0; non-negative unchanged.
Output beat count equals M and out_last asserted only on final beat.
verification: Minimum 100 randomized legal transactions across varying M,N within bounds.
Include reset tests from active processing and idle.
Include backpressure tests on both input and output ready/valid.
Include illegal config tests (M=0, N=0, M>MAX_M, N>MAX_N) and verify ERROR behavior/recovery.
Check exact transfer ordering and counts for CFG/X/A/BIAS sections.
rtl: SystemVerilog synthesizable subset only; no forbidden constructs.
Ready/valid rule enforced: transfer iff ready&&valid, stable payload during stall.
Parameterization must elaborate for defaults LANES=16, MAX_M=256, MAX_N=256.
fpga_handoff: Vivado synthesis results accepted only from deterministic tool report per provided schema.
RTL verification must pass before synthesis handoff.

diagnosis.root_cause: Primary defect is in mv_npu_top control/datapath integration: cfg_m/cfg_n and bias/relu enables are decoded from wrong bit positions, compute starts immediately on cfg without enforcing section sequencing, row/output progress is driven by a_lane_valid rather than FSM-defined completion, and output emission does not honor backpressure/row-finalize protocol. This produces early divergence (output count/data mismatch) and later deadlock/timeouts.

first_divergence.expected: Exactly M outputs with correct dot/bias/relu values and final out_last
first_divergence.observed: Example failure shows len(out)=10 vs expected 8; other tests hit job timeout

evidence.observation: Assertion failure: len(out)=10 while expected M=8
evidence.relevance: Direct violation of architectural invariant exactly one output per row
Control/progress protocol can stall or fail to complete jobs

evidence.observation: pack_cfg encodes M in bits[7:0], N in bits[15:8], bias_en bit16, relu_en bit17

evidence.relevance: Deterministic decode mismatch against frozen verifier contract

evidence.observation: Top drives compute_active/start_row locally and ignores ctrl_fsm pulses for sequencing; out emission tied inside a_lane_valid/col_idx path
evidence.relevance: Explains output duplication/loss and timeout under stalls

evidence.observation: Only WIDTHEXPAND warnings, no fatal compile/elab errors
evidence.relevance: Confirms failure is functional simulation, not compile-time

alternative_hypotheses: x_buffer_mem read latency misalignment contributes to arithmetic mismatch
output_if may drop in_valid pulses if producer protocol is violated upstream

repair_plan.recommended_change: 1) Fix cfg decode in mv_npu_top to match frozen verifier encoding (M[7:0], N[15:8], bias_en[16], relu_en[17]) with proper zero-extension to MW/NW. 2) Rework control so job progression follows contract sections and FSM pulses: load X first, then consume A for exactly M*N elements, finalize exactly once per row, optional bias per row only when enabled, emit exactly M outputs in row order. 3) Gate counter/state advances strictly on ready&&valid handshakes; hold output payload/valid during out_ready=0; prevent duplicate finalize/output on stalls. 4) Ensure illegal cfg handling and recovery semantics in ctrl_fsm: status_err latches in ERROR for invalid bounds and clears on next legal cfg accept; busy reflects active legal job only. 5) Align top-level start_row/step_valid/out_in_valid generation with FSM-defined compute_step/row_finalize/job_done events rather than raw in_beat acceptance.
do_not_change: Do not modify frozen tests or reference model
Do not change module interfaces or signal widths at top level
Do not alter arithmetic semantics (INT8 signed multiply, INT32 wrap, optional bias, optional ReLU)
Do not change input section ordering contract
expected_side_effects: Cycle timing/latency per job may shift to contract-compliant behavior
Width warnings may reduce after cfg decode correction

rtl_result.summary: Repair requires coherent redesign of top/FSM sequencing around section-aware handshakes and row-finalize timing, but available module interfaces do not provide sufficient control/observation signals (e.g., explicit section progress, A-consume acknowledge, bias-consume acknowledge, output-buffer availability) to deterministically enforce frozen sequencing/invariants without risking architectural reinterpretation.

contract_checks.requirement: Change only affected modules and preserve frozen interfaces
contract_checks.evidence: No files changed; protected modules/interfaces untouched.

contract_checks.requirement: Do not silently alter architecture when evidence is insufficient
contract_checks.evidence: Blocked instead of introducing speculative FSM/top protocol behavior.

contract_checks.requirement: Ready/valid and exact section/count sequencing must be enforced
contract_checks.evidence: Current available ports between mv_npu_top and ctrl_fsm are insufficient to unambiguously encode required section-consumption progress and one-finalize-per-row behavior under stalls.

rtl_result.blocked_reason: Insufficient deterministic repair authority at current interfaces: ctrl_fsm lacks required observability/controls for section-level accepted-beat accounting (X/A/BIAS), row completion gating tied to actual accepted A beats and xmem latency alignment, and explicit coupling to output_if availability to prevent duplicate/missed finalize under backpressure. Implementing these semantics without additional contract-level signals would require speculative architectural reinterpretation.
known_risks: If patched speculatively, may still violate exact M outputs and stall safety under randomized backpressure.
Potential off-by-one/latency coupling errors around x_buffer 1-cycle read and MAC step accounting.

import random
import cocotb
from cocotb.triggers import Timer, SimTimeoutError
from reference.mv_npu_ref import mv_job, s8, s32, sanity_checks

TYPE_CFG = 0
TYPE_X = 1
TYPE_A = 2
TYPE_B = 3

MAX_M = 256
MAX_N = 256
SEED = 20260911


def pack_cfg(m, n, bias_en, relu_en):
    # cfg_word on 32-bit ingress beat per frozen contract usage
    return ((relu_en & 1) << 17) | ((bias_en & 1) << 16) | ((n & 0xFF) << 8) | (m & 0xFF)


async def cycle(dut, in_drive=None, out_ready=1):
    dut.clk.value = 0
    if in_drive is None:
        dut.in_valid.value = 0
        dut.in_data.value = 0
        dut.in_type.value = 0
        dut.in_last.value = 0
    else:
        dut.in_valid.value = in_drive["valid"]
        dut.in_data.value = in_drive["data"]
        dut.in_type.value = in_drive["type"]
        dut.in_last.value = in_drive["last"]
    dut.out_ready.value = out_ready
    await Timer(1, units="ns")
    in_hs = int(dut.in_valid.value) and int(dut.in_ready.value)
    out_hs = int(dut.out_valid.value) and int(dut.out_ready.value)
    out_data = s32(int(dut.out_data.value)) if int(dut.out_valid.value) else None
    out_last = int(dut.out_last.value) if int(dut.out_valid.value) else 0
    dut.clk.value = 1
    await Timer(1, units="ns")
    dut.clk.value = 0
    await Timer(1, units="ns")
    return in_hs, out_hs, out_data, out_last, int(dut.status_err.value), int(dut.busy.value)


async def apply_reset(dut, cycles=3):
    dut.rst_n.value = 0
    for _ in range(cycles):
        await cycle(dut, None, 0)
    dut.rst_n.value = 1
    await cycle(dut, None, 1)


async def send_beat_hold_until_hs(dut, beat, out_ready_fn):
    while True:
        _, _, _, _, _, _ = await cycle(dut, beat, out_ready_fn())
        if int(dut.in_ready.value) and beat["valid"]:
            break


async def run_job(dut, cfg, x, a, b, out_ready_fn, src_idle_rng):
    beats = []
    beats.append({"valid": 1, "data": pack_cfg(cfg['M'], cfg['N'], cfg['bias_en'], cfg['relu_en']), "type": TYPE_CFG, "last": 1})
    for i, xv in enumerate(x):
        beats.append({"valid": 1, "data": (s8(xv) & 0xFF), "type": TYPE_X, "last": 1 if i == len(x)-1 else 0})
    flat_a = [v for row in a for v in row]
    for i, av in enumerate(flat_a):
        beats.append({"valid": 1, "data": (s8(av) & 0xFF), "type": TYPE_A, "last": 1 if i == len(flat_a)-1 else 0})
    if cfg["bias_en"]:
        for i, bv in enumerate(b):
            beats.append({"valid": 1, "data": (s32(bv) & 0xFFFFFFFF), "type": TYPE_B, "last": 1 if i == len(b)-1 else 0})

    exp = mv_job(cfg, x, a, b if cfg["bias_en"] else None)

    out = []
    idx = 0
    wait_cycles = 0
    while idx < len(beats) or len(out) < cfg["M"]:
        if idx < len(beats) and src_idle_rng.randint(0, 3) == 0:
            in_drive = None
        elif idx < len(beats):
            in_drive = beats[idx]
        else:
            in_drive = None

        in_hs, out_hs, out_data, out_last, _, _ = await cycle(dut, in_drive, out_ready_fn())
        if in_drive is not None and in_hs:
            idx += 1
        if out_hs:
            out.append((out_data, out_last))

        wait_cycles += 1
        if wait_cycles > 50000:
            raise SimTimeoutError("job timeout")

    assert len(out) == cfg["M"], f"output count mismatch exp={cfg['M']} got={len(out)}"
    for i, (d, l) in enumerate(out):
        assert d == exp[i], f"row {i} mismatch exp={exp[i]} got={d}"
        assert l == (1 if i == cfg["M"]-1 else 0), f"out_last mismatch row={i}"


@cocotb.test()
async def test_smoke_directed(dut):
    sanity_checks()
    await apply_reset(dut)
    cfg = {"M": 2, "N": 3, "bias_en": 1, "relu_en": 1}
    x = [1, -2, 3]
    a = [[4, 5, -6], [-1, -1, -1]]
    b = [7, -100]
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    await run_job(dut, cfg, x, a, b, out_ready_fn=lambda: 1, src_idle_rng=rng)


@cocotb.test()
async def test_reset_idle_and_active(dut):
    await apply_reset(dut)
    assert int(dut.status_err.value) == 0
    cfg = {"M": 4, "N": 5, "bias_en": 0, "relu_en": 0}
    x = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    a = [[1, 0, 0, 0, 0] for _ in range(4)]
    b = []
    rng = random.Random(SEED + 1)
    await run_job(dut, cfg, x, a, b, out_ready_fn=lambda: 1, src_idle_rng=rng)
    await apply_reset(dut)


@cocotb.test()
async def test_backpressure_in_out(dut):
    await apply_reset(dut)
    cfg = {"M": 8, "N": 17, "bias_en": 1, "relu_en": 0}
    rng = random.Random(SEED + 2)
    x = [rng.randint(-128, 127) for _ in range(cfg["N"])]
    a = [[rng.randint(-128, 127) for _ in range(cfg["N"])] for _ in range(cfg["M"])]
    b = [rng.randint(-(1<<31), (1<<31)-1) for _ in range(cfg["M"])]
    out_rng = random.Random(SEED + 3)
    await run_job(dut, cfg, x, a, b, out_ready_fn=lambda: 1 if out_rng.randint(0, 2) else 0, src_idle_rng=rng)


@cocotb.test()
async def test_illegal_cfg_error_recovery(dut):
    await apply_reset(dut)
    illegal = [pack_cfg(0, 4, 0, 0), pack_cfg(4, 0, 0, 0), pack_cfg(255, 1, 0, 0)]
    for w in illegal:
        beat = {"valid": 1, "data": w, "type": TYPE_CFG, "last": 1}
        await send_beat_hold_until_hs(dut, beat, lambda: 1)
        for _ in range(3):
            _, _, _, _, err, _ = await cycle(dut, None, 1)
        assert err == 1, "status_err must assert for illegal cfg"

    cfg = {"M": 1, "N": 1, "bias_en": 0, "relu_en": 0}
    x = [2]
    a = [[3]]
    await run_job(dut, cfg, x, a, [], out_ready_fn=lambda: 1, src_idle_rng=random.Random(SEED + 4))
    assert int(dut.status_err.value) == 0, "status_err must clear after legal cfg accept"


@cocotb.test()
async def test_randomized_100(dut):
    await apply_reset(dut)
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    for t in range(100):
        m = rng.randint(1, 16)
        n = rng.randint(1, 32)
        cfg = {
            "M": m,
            "N": n,
            "bias_en": rng.randint(0, 1),
            "relu_en": rng.randint(0, 1),
        }
        x = [rng.randint(-128, 127) for _ in range(n)]
        a = [[rng.randint(-128, 127) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(m)]
        b = [rng.randint(-(1<<31), (1<<31)-1) for _ in range(m)] if cfg["bias_en"] else []
        out_rng = random.Random(SEED + 1000 + t)
        await run_job(dut, cfg, x, a, b, out_ready_fn=lambda: 1 if out_rng.randint(0, 3) else 0, src_idle_rng=rng)

diagnosis.root_cause: Primary defect is in mv_npu_top control/datapath integration: cfg_m/cfg_n and bias/relu enables are decoded from wrong bit positions, compute starts immediately on cfg without enforcing section sequencing, row/output progress is driven by a_lane_valid rather than FSM-defined completion, and output emission does not honor backpressure/row-finalize protocol. This produces early divergence (output count/data mismatch) and later deadlock/timeouts.

evidence.relevance: Explains output duplication/loss and timeout under stalls

repair_plan.recommended_change: 1) Fix cfg decode in mv_npu_top to match frozen verifier encoding (M[7:0], N[15:8], bias_en[16], relu_en[17]) with proper zero-extension to MW/NW. 2) Rework control so job progression follows contract sections and FSM pulses: load X first, then consume A for exactly M*N elements, finalize exactly once per row, optional bias per row only when enabled, emit exactly M outputs in row order. 3) Gate counter/state advances strictly on ready&&valid handshakes; hold output payload/valid during out_ready=0; prevent duplicate finalize/output on stalls. 4) Ensure illegal cfg handling and recovery semantics in ctrl_fsm: status_err latches in ERROR for invalid bounds and clears on next legal cfg accept; busy reflects active legal job only. 5) Align top-level start_row/step_valid/out_in_valid generation with FSM-defined compute_step/row_finalize/job_done events rather than raw in_beat acceptance.
